text.p: Following are the main stories in Wednesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Computer Crimes Bill and Digital Signature Bill were tabled in Parliament on Tuesday. The two Bills are part of a set of cyberlaws drafted to provide a legal framework for the creation of the Multimedia Super Corridor.
- Former Australian Prime Minister Bob Hawke praises Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad for being one of the most successful leaders in the world.
- Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim criticises financial institutions for their refusal to provide capital to aspiring young businessmen.
- Anwar urges the Anti-Corruption Agency to continue investigating allegations of corruption in road construction projects.
- Telekom Malaysia expects to spend between 500 million and one billion ringgit this year to provide telecommunications infrastructure to property development projects.
